question: When did the second urbanisation in Ganga Valley take place?
solution:
The correct answer is __**6th Century BCE**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The second urbanisation in the Ganga Valley took place during the **6th Century BCE**.
 
• This period marked the rise of large cities and the establishment of powerful kingdoms and republics in the region.
 
• It was characterized by significant advancements in trade, economy, and culture.
 
• The period saw the emergence of important cities such as Varanasi, Pataliputra, and Rajagriha.
 
• It also witnessed the rise of major religious movements including Buddhism and Jainism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The first urbanisation in the Indian subcontinent is associated with the Indus Valley Civilization, which flourished around 2500 BCE.
 
• The second urbanisation period is noted for the development of the Mahajanapadas, which were large territorial states.
 
• Key factors contributing to this urbanisation included the use of iron tools and weapons, which facilitated agricultural expansion and military conquests.
 
• The period also saw the compilation of significant literary works such as the Upanishads and other early Buddhist texts.
